title: a bound's omission marker is suppressed when --fields projects it away (task list and task view)
description:
BLOCKED on opum-doc's ruling on the DEC-3 semantic 3 vs --fields collision (routed by the orchestrator as an A/B at about 02:35Z, 2026-10-06: A = the omission marker survives projection, emitted beside the projected data whenever a bound is supplied; B = projection wins and DEC-3's wording is scoped to unprojected output). Do NOT start until that answer lands.

Reported by the QCLI-291 round-2 independent review (wf_f7e8997d-b28), and reachable identically on task list --fields (shipped in opum-ai/quest-cli#518). DEC-3 semantic 3 says a supplied bound always reports its omission; --fields says data carries exactly the named keys. The two collide when a caller supplies --max-notes AND a --fields set that omits notesOmitted.

EXACT REPRO (quest on dev after #519): quest task view <id> --max-notes 0 --fields implementationNotes --json returns data {implementationNotes: []} with NO notesOmitted, while quest task view <id> --max-notes 0 --json returns notesOmitted:1. task list carries no omission marker for --limit at all today, so the same shape is reachable there.

Scope covers BOTH commands so that whichever shape is ruled is applied once, not twice.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The ruled shape is implemented for BOTH task list and task view, so a caller that supplies a bound and a --fields set can always tell a partial read from a complete one -- or the ruling explicitly scopes DEC-3 semantic 3 to unprojected output and the help and guide say so
A test pins the decided bound-plus-projection behaviour on both commands
